task.question: Improve the period loss in finite RMS/short-moment transfer and retain an exact global-phase obstruction.
task.domain: Supplied periodic conjugation-invariant cell models, not actual zeta zeros.
assumptions: Q is a positive integer; m in {0,1,2}; sum m=Q; one supplied center p+tau_p per occupied unit cell, tau in [0,1).
0<=a_p<=A<infinity; a_p=0 for m_p!=2. L_alpha is the precisely normalized periodic spectral expression in proof.md (1).
RMS transfer allows s=0; use of the inherited anchor estimate and the improved defect tradeoff requires s>0.
For growing-Q corollaries the depth cap is uniform and s tends to 2/3; the short arithmetic-style budget is an additional hypothesis, not an actual-zeta theorem.

exact_subchecks: 480 rational rounding assignments (cap tested even at mean load two)
Period-six rational energy 398/243 and rational constants 1/128 and 53/972; the all-Q trigonometric identities are proved separately, not by Fraction.
methods: Operator/RMS/centered short-moment regressions, including collisions and s=0 boundaries
Cyclic strain samples Q=18,36,72,144,288,576 and a finite phase grid
limitations: No proof of RH or improved unconditional proportion of zeta zeros.
No extraction of the supplied cell/periodic representation from actual zeros or an arbitrary small signed defect.
No period-independent two-scale separation, source weights/localization transfer, or exceptional operator-energy control.
Numerical tests and exact finite checks do not verify the universal analytic quantifiers.
No independent-verifier receipt, upstream Lean build, or full-repository local test run.
The global-phase counterexample fails the short budget; it is not a counterexample to a period-free two-scale theorem.
The new conservative threshold is weaker than the old one for some small Q; only its growth order improves.
